A0178.title: AIoT Model Security Protection
A0178.description: Implement adversarial example defense, data poisoning detection, model integrity verification, and inference anomaly monitoring for AIoT edge-side models to ensure decision reliability, preventing attackers from causing the device to make incorrect judgments through adversarial perturbations, poisoned training data, or model replacement.
A0178.definition: Defend AI models against adversarial examples and poisoning attacks to ensure decision reliability.
A0178.limitation: Adversarial training only covers known perturbation patterns; novel adversarial examples (black-box attacks, physical-world perturbations) can still deceive the model and bypass defenses. Poisoning detection suffers from high false-negative rates at large data scales, making slow injection-style poisoning difficult to detect. Limited edge-side computing power constrains the deployment of heavily defended models, creating a trade-off between defense strength and inference latency. Model theft and model substitution attacks can construct adversarial examples without access to the original model, rendering defenses ineffective.
